routes.label: Combine the reciprocal sums before multiplying

question: For all positive numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z,\) the product \[ \begin{aligned} &(x+y+z)^{-1}\\ &\quad\cdot(x^{-1}+y^{-1}+z^{-1})\\ &\quad\cdot(xy+yz+zx)^{-1}\\ &\quad\cdot\big((xy)^{-1}+(yz)^{-1}+(zx)^{-1}\big) \end{aligned} \] equals
solution:
Use \(a^{-1}=1/a\) and give each reciprocal sum the common denominator \(xyz\). This exposes the sums appearing in the other factors:
\[
\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z
=\frac{xy+yz+zx}{xyz},
\]
\[
\frac1{xy}+\frac1{yz}+\frac1{zx}
=\frac{x+y+z}{xyz}.
\]
In the original product, these numerators cancel \(xy+yz+zx\) and \(x+y+z\) from the other two factors. Positivity of \(x,y,z\) ensures that every denominator and canceled factor is nonzero. What remains is
\[
\frac1{(xyz)^2}
=\frac1{x^2y^2z^2}
=x^{-2}y^{-2}z^{-2}.
\]
Therefore the answer is \(x^{-2}y^{-2}z^{-2}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
